newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle not well established-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle not well established-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow late Monday afternoon, with not enough sold to establish a market, feedlot sources said.
About 100 steers likely to grade mostly select sold in Kansas at $63.00 per cwt but the sales were not for the same quality that sold last week at $63.00, they said.
Select- and choice-type cattle generally were priced by owners at $64.00 to $65.00, with a few at $66.00 after some cattle feeders passed bids at $62.00 to $63.00, sources said.
Fed cattle prices were seen underpinned this week by firm beef prices and current feedlot marketings, they said.
Beef prices on Monday climbed $1.58 to $1.82 per cwt on 142 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.

Beef values were higher amid tight stocks following active beef sales the last two weeks and firm demand from retailers for end of the month and pre-Independence Day holiday promotions, market sources said.
Showlists this week were estimated near 81,500 head for the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, up 2,000 from last week and near 92,500 in Kansas, up 3,500, sources in those areas said.
